companyDescription: Sidewalk delivery robotics · ~2,000-robot fleet across 20 cities · Uber Eats/DoorDash/Nvidia/White Castle partnerships + Diligent Robotics healthcare acquisition · trading near its 52-week low
priceNote: Self-fetched today (no live-prices.json cache yet). Trading at $5.38, barely above the 52-week low ($5.02) and down sharply from the $18.64 high — the stock is down ~16% YTD despite the fleet more than doubling this year, a disconnect between operating progress and price the Aug 6 print will have to address.
summary: Serve Robotics reports Q2 2026 earnings on Aug 6, 2026, sitting just above its 52-week low even as the fleet scaled to ~2,000 robots across 20 cities and 6 metro areas, with 2026 revenue guidance raised to ~$26M. This is a real growth story trading at a depressed multiple: Q1 2026 revenue was up 578% YoY, but a GAAP miss and expansion-investment spend drove a post-earnings selloff, and the stock's own earnings-day history is genuinely mixed (+12.3% last beat, -3% last miss). All 8 covering analysts rate it Strong Buy with an $18.45 average target (+243% from here) — one of the widest upside gaps in this screen, backed by real partnerships (Uber Eats, DoorDash, Nvidia, White Castle) and the Diligent Robotics healthcare diversification. Small-cap, pre-profitability, and genuinely volatile around earnings — speculative sizing only.

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Serve reports Aug 6, 2026. The company's own earnings-day history is a coin flip — Q4 2025 results drove a +12.3% pop, but the May 2026 Q1 print fell over 3% on a GAAP net loss miss despite 578% YoY revenue growth. The market needs to see expansion spend translating into narrowing losses, not just faster top-line growth.

catalysts.name: Fleet Scale-Up to 2,000+ Robots
catalysts.description: Fleet has reached ~2,000 robots across 20 cities and 6 metro areas (44 cities/14 states including Diligent's footprint), with 2026 revenue guidance raised to ~$26M — an ongoing operational proof point ahead of the Q2 print.

catalysts.name: Diligent Robotics Healthcare Diversification
catalysts.description: The Diligent Robotics acquisition pushes Serve beyond food delivery into hospital service robotics — a diversification story that could re-rate the stock if it starts showing up materially in the revenue mix this year.

risks: Stock is near its 52-week low despite the fleet more than doubling this year — the market is discounting execution/cash-burn risk over growth, and Aug 6 needs to change that narrative
Own earnings-day history is genuinely mixed: +12.3% on the last beat (Mar 2026) but -3%+ on the last miss (May 2026), with a historical average earnings-day move of roughly -4%

Pre-profitability with a GAAP net loss that missed consensus last quarter — expansion spend (new markets, Diligent integration) needs to show a path to narrowing losses, not just faster revenue growth
Consensus target ($18.45) implies more than a 3x move — even the low end of the analyst range ($13, +142%) requires a lot of good news to materialize
Competition from well-capitalized players (DoorDash's own robotics efforts) in the same delivery-robotics space

estimateDates.note: Market wants to see expansion spend narrowing losses, not just top-line growth
estimateDates.est: Revenue growth expected to continue; profitability trajectory is the swing factor

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed holds at 3.50–3.75%, but new Chair Warsh's hawkish tone has 9 of 18 officials projecting a further 2026 hike, with the next FOMC decision Jul 28–29, 2026 — just days after this report.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Core inflation remains above target and the 10-year yield sits near 4.48% — a real headwind for a pre-profitability small-cap that needs continued access to capital to fund fleet expansion.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: As an unprofitable small-cap growth name, SERV is among the more rate-sensitive picks in this screen — higher-for-longer compresses the valuation multiple the market is willing to pay for its growth, on top of the existing execution-risk discount.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM-HIGH — this is one of the more macro-sensitive names in this screen given its pre-profitability status and reliance on continued capital access; a hawkish surprise at the Jul 28-29 FOMC would compound the stock's existing near-52-week-low weakness.
